plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that produces goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers directly from the ground in autumn, long after its broad strap-like leaves have withered in early summer. The leafless blooms appear to emerge from bare soil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to October in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of Europe, widely cultivated in gardens in temperate regions
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxin that is also used by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling and in medicine to treat gout.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, robust perennial with hairy stems and dense clusters of daisy-like flower heads with golden-yellow centers and many narrow ray petals. It is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Prairies, meadows and roadsides of eastern and central North America
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies rely heavily on its nectar to fuel their long migration to Mexico during October.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A graceful, semi-deciduous tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often before leaves fully emerge. Streets and parks are carpeted with fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; planted widely in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Sydney, Brisbane) and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, which is known as the Jacaranda City, there are roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, and a folk belief says a falling blossom on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: An airy annual with feathery foliage and saucer-shaped daisy-like flowers on slender stems. It thrives in sun and poor soil, blooming prolifically until the first frost.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to first frost (July to October in temperate Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Mexico; cultivated and naturalized across North America, Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from the Greek word 'kosmos' meaning order or harmony, a name given by Spanish priests who grew them in mission gardens in Mexico.
